en: I, Jñānagupta, take refuge in the Great Ocean of Wisdom, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Supreme Lamp-King of the East.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra of the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Supreme Lamp-King of the East*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty, together with others.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of assemblies of bodhisattvas,
as well as immeasurable assemblies of devas and humans,
namely Mahābrahmā and Śakradevendra.
The Four Great Heavenly Kings,
namely: the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka,
the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa.
Led by the Great Deity Guṇadhara,
there were eighty-four thousand hosts of devas;
led by the Great General Nāyaya, [there were...]
The great generals of the eight classes of spirits and ghosts,
as well as five hundred Mother-of-Ghosts (Hārītī) with their retinues—
thus surrounded on all sides by immeasurable multitudes of devas, humans, and worldly beings.
At that time, beyond hundreds of thousands of billions of buddha-fields from this buddha-field,
there was a buddha-field in the eastern direction named the World of Boundless Flowers.
In that world, there was a buddha.
He is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Supreme Lamp,
who currently dwells in ease preaching the Dharma.
That Tathāgata has dispatched two bodhisattvas from that world.
Having come to this Sahā world,
two bodhisattvas— one named Mahāprabha and the other named Amṛtaprabha— spoke, saying:
"You two bodhisattvas, go toward the Sahā world."
In that [world] there is a Buddha named Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
[it was] for the sake of that Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
I shall now recite these dhāraṇī verses for the sake of all sentient beings, for their peace and happiness,
and for the sake of merit and increase.
Because of renown, because of the arising of power,
because of acting according to one's will, because of experiencing peace and happiness,
because of being undisturbed, because of not killing sentient beings, and because of providing protection.
And he spoke the mantra, saying: *Tad upādāni*.
Dūṇire khānu-gopate parajavale jhavale jhavale mahājhavale.
Jambū-laṅkate jambule jambulini.
Mahājāvarī jāvara mukhi sāri.
Masalī akale makale.
Ākṣi-mākṣi-nākṣi-sāvale mahāsāvale saphale.
The Samādhi of the Phrases and the Sentences.
Mahā-samādhi-te samādhi mahā-samādhi mahā-jāvale se.
Sarami mukhi śami mahāśami.
Samādhi mahāsamādhi trimukhe vimukhe arase.
Mahā-araśmi-mana-śi-ma-na-śi.
*Manase tibeṭi svāhā.* At that time, those two bodhisattvas, having received and upheld this dhāraṇī...
Just as it takes a strong man the time to bend and extend his arm,
in that same manner, the Bodhisattva vanished from that World of Boundless Flowers and arrived at the Jeta Grove,
Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, in the city of Śrāvastī.
At present, the Bodhisattva went to the presence of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
having arrived, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
Having circumambulated [the Buddha] three times, he stood to one side.
Standing there, that bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, beyond eight thousand billion buddha-fields from this buddha-field..."
In the eastern direction there is a world named Boundless Flower.
In that world there is a Buddha named Supreme Lamp, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Now, while I am preaching the Dharma for him,
that Blessed One, the Most Excellent Lamp Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha— [is present].
He has sent us here to this Sahā world.
That Buddha Supreme Lamp inquires after the World-Honored One,
asking whether you have little illness and little affliction, whether your daily life is light and easy, and whether your strength is at peace.
Again he spoke these words:
"The World-Honored One has no disturbances among his followers,
whether the assembly of bhikṣus or the assembly of bhikṣuṇīs."
The assembly of upāsakas and the assembly of upāsikās;
or humans, or non-humans;
or devas, or nāgas, or yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
Or great ghost generals, or kumbhāṇḍas;
or kumbhāṇḍa spirit generals, or pūtanas;
or piśācas, or hungry ghosts, or māyā-ghosts.
Or centipedes, or venomous snakes,
or vipers and scorpions, or various other poisonous insects,
or asuras such as Rāhula.
Or *sagandha* ghosts, or *pipāsā* (thirst) ghosts,
or fainting ghosts, or disease ghosts;
or those practicing sorcery, or corpses.
Whether it be fevers occurring on the first day, second day, third day, or fourth day,
or other various disturbances caused by demonic afflictions,
they shall not cause such disturbances.
The Tathāgata Varapradīpa has sent us to bring this dhāraṇī mantra for the benefit of all sentient beings and for their nourishment.
For the sake of increasing merit, for the sake of increasing majestic power,
for the sake of increasing physical beauty, for the sake of producing renown,
for the sake of increasing strength, and for the sake of experiencing pleasure according to one's wishes.
Because they experience peace and happiness accordingly,
and because it prevents disturbance and provides protection,
he recited the aforementioned mantra.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Elder Ānanda, saying:
"Ānanda, you should receive and uphold these verses of this dhāraṇī;
having received them, explain, expound, and disseminate them for others."
Ānanda, it is difficult for a Buddha to appear in the world, and difficult to hear or encounter him.
This dharani chapter and its phrases are even more difficult to hear.
If there are good sons or good daughters...
Whoever is able to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī—
whether by reading it, reciting it, or explaining and proclaiming it to others—
that person cannot be burned by fire nor harmed by weapons.
No poisons can harm them, no officials can execute them,
and Brahmā does not become angry with them.
For seven lifetimes, such a person constantly knows their past lives.
Ānanda, these dharani verses were spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past.
Should anyone slander this mantra, [they will incur great retribution].
They shall immediately slander those Buddhas.
If there are spirits or deities who do not revere this mantra,
or who would seize the power of such-and-such a person from me, [may they be destroyed].
If there are those who have already used incantations to seize [the merit] and do not return it,
the heads of those spirits and deities shall split into seven pieces.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ajita—
Rising from his seat, he adjusted his robes,
bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground,
and addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One."
I also proclaim these dharani verses for the sake of sentient beings receiving benefit,
for their increase, and for the augmentation of their merit.
Because it increases power, increases physical form, and increases renown;
because by increasing power one experiences pleasure in accordance with one's conduct;
because one experiences assistance and joy in accordance with what is practiced; and because there is no disturbance.
Because it prevents slaughter and provides protection,
he spoke this mantra:

*Tadyathā | Adite | Vadite | Nādike | Kūṇāde | Akavade | Parāvade | Dvolumi | Hululumi | Anākase | Panākase | Kākase | Mahākase | Anutapārase | Vikakhi | Mahākakhi | Sṭabhi | Ṭaṭabhi | Khiri | Miri | Tirī | Śirī | Pūrṣi | Mahāpūrṣi | Pūrpūrṣi | Pūrṣavade | Svāhā.* At that time, the Buddha addressed the Elder Ānanda, saying:
You should receive these dharani verses and mantras;
constantly uphold, recite, and read them,
and explain them to others, proclaiming and disseminating them far and wide.
Ānanda, it is difficult to encounter a Buddha appearing in the world;
to hear this dhāraṇī is twice as difficult.
If there are good sons or good daughters, [who...]
They will also be able to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī;
having received it, they will be able to maintain, read, and recite it,
and they will be able to proclaim, disseminate, and explain it for the sake of others.
That person will be able to know the events of fourteen future kalpas.
Ānanda, these dharani verses were spoken by eighty-four billion buddhas of the past.
If there is anyone who slanders this dhāraṇī and does not believe in its practice,
that person slanders all the Buddhas of the past;
such a person turns their back on and abandons all the Buddhas.
If there are beings of any kind who seize the vital essence of such-and-such a person of mine,
or having seized it do not return it,
those persons shall also incur such transgressions as these.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī rose from his seat,
adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
I, too, shall proclaim these dhāraṇī verses for the benefit of sentient beings,
for their peace and happiness, and for the increase of their merit.
Because it increases majestic power; because it increases physical form;
because it increases renown; because it increases strength;
because one experiences pleasure according to one's wishes; and because one experiences peace and happiness in accordance with one's conduct.
Because it does not cause disturbance, because it does not kill or harm, and because it provides protection,
he spoke this mantra:

*Tadyathā | ākṣama akṣaṇakharasena kiṇi nāgasale | bharaniṇe | cakṣile | cakṣiravate | caṇḍale caṇḍaravate | jākṣile jākṣiravate | candile candiravate | svāhā.* Then the Buddha addressed the Elder Ānanda.
Ānanda, you should receive this dhāraṇī;
constantly uphold, recite, and read it,
and explain, propagate, and disseminate it for others.
Ānanda, it is difficult for a Buddha to appear in the world;
to hear this dhāraṇī is twice as difficult.
If there is anyone who can receive and uphold this dhāraṇī, [it is even more rare].
It is even more difficult than that,
Ānanda. If there are sons or daughters of good family who are able to receive this dhāraṇī...
Having received it, one is able to maintain, recite, and explain it to others for their benefit;
such a person will be able to know the events of seven future lifetimes.
Ānanda, this is the dharani chapter.
This was spoken by ninety billion Buddhas of the past.
If there is anyone who slanders this dhāraṇī and does not believe or practice it,
that person thereby slanders those Buddhas of the past.
Such a person would be abandoning those Buddhas.
If there are any classes of beings who seize the vital essence of me, [named] so-and-so,
and having seized it, do not return it.
Such a person shall likewise incur such transgressions.
At that time, Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha,
addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"O bhikṣus, I shall now also proclaim the dhāraṇī verses for the benefit of sentient beings,
for their peace and happiness, and for the increase of their merit."
Because it increases majestic power; because it increases physical form;
because it increases renown; because it increases strength;
because one experiences pleasure according to one's wishes; and because one experiences peace and happiness in accordance with one's conduct.
Because it does not disturb, because it does not harm, and because it protects,
he spoke this mantra:
*tadyathā*...
Ajñānajñānakovidānugatacāraṇabhadranirbhaya-dhīra-bhadra-durdhara.
Eya āra va kīṭa kīṭa cakra-lu-me hulu-me śre.
Mahāśrīkṣame mahākṣame lire.
Lū-ri-le, kṣi-le, ji-le,
kṣi-khu-er-fan-le, mi-le.

Śiśili śīlavadhi āsthā sthāna sthiku sthāna sthāne.
Aṇavate panavate akase makase kase kasakase phase.
Phra-se mahā-phra-se ī-ni-mai-ni.
*Tatṭe tatṭe paratatṭe taptatṭe svāhā.* At that time,
the Buddha addressed the Elder Ānanda.
Ānanda, you should receive this dhāraṇī;
constantly uphold, recite, and read it,
and explain it to others, proclaiming and disseminating it far and wide.
Ānanda, it is difficult for a Buddha to appear in the world;
to hear this dhāraṇī is even more difficult still.
If there be anyone who can receive and uphold this dhāraṇī, [it is most rare].
It is even more difficult than that,
Ānanda. If there are sons or daughters of good family who are able to receive this dhāraṇī.
Having received it, they are able to uphold, read, and recite it,
and are able to proclaim, disseminate, and explain it to others.
Such a person can know the events of twenty-one future lifetimes.
Ānanda, these dharani verses were spoken by ninety-nine billion Buddhas of the past.
If there should be anyone who slanders this dharani and does not believe or practice it, [they will incur great suffering].
That person would thereby slander those past Buddhas;
that person would thereby abandon those Buddhas.
If there are any classes of beings who seize the vital essence of me, [named] So-and-so...
If one seizes [an object] and does not return it,
that person likewise incurs such a transgression.
Ānanda, if there be sons or daughters of good family...
If one upholds these dharani verses and,
taking even a withered tree,
performs the rite of boundary-binding (sīmābandha) for protection and recites the mantra, [the tree will be restored].
If it can even cause branches, twigs, flowers, leaves, and fruit to grow upon a withered tree,
how much more so for a sentient being with consciousness who upholds this mantra—
would it not be impossible for such a person not to be cured?
I take refuge in all Buddhas.
May I achieve success with this mantra: svāhā.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"O Bhikṣus, I shall now further proclaim the dhāraṇī verses for the sake of benefit,
peace, and happiness, for the increase of merit,
and for the attainment of majesty, physical strength, renown, and ease according to one's wishes."
Because it constantly provides protection without producing affliction or harm,
he spoke this mantra:

*Tadyathā | āve āve | ṭaḥ | keṭara keṭalu mate | dharu mate | dhure dhuradhure | bhare | sare | dhure dhure | dhudhure | sūre | bhaṇihe | bhaṇili | khili | phili | tiri svāhā.* At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
Ānanda, you should receive and uphold these dharani verses.
Having upheld them, recite and chant them, explain them to others, and propagate them far and wide.
Ānanda, it is difficult for a Buddha to appear in the world.
To hear this dhāraṇī is twice as difficult;
for one to recite and uphold this dhāraṇī is twice as difficult again.
Ānanda, if there are sons or daughters of good family who receive and uphold these dharani phrases,
and having received and upheld them, read, recite, explain them to others, and propagate them;
That person will come to know the events of twenty-eight lifetimes.
Ānanda, these verses of this dhāraṇī were spoken by as many Buddhas of the past as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
If anyone slanders this mantra,
they are thereby slandering those Buddhas;
such a person has abandoned those Buddhas.
If there are any beings who seize the vital essence of my [name],
and having seized it, do not return it,
those persons shall also incur such a transgression.
If there is a mantra-practitioner who casts spells upon another person,
all the curses and incantations that person possesses will be unable to cause harm.
One may employ this mantra to protect others.
That person cannot be harmed by any of the devas;
they cannot be harmed by any of the nāgas;
they cannot be harmed by any yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kinnaras, mahoragas, or garuḍas.
No rākṣasas shall be able to harm them;
no officials shall be able to cause them harm;
and no bandits shall be able to cause them harm.
No humans or non-humans can cause them harm.
No venomous snakes or poisonous insects can cause them harm.
No vipers or scorpions can cause them harm.
No boils, nor any fevers such as cold-fevers or hot-fevers, can cause harm;
no malarial fevers occurring on the first, second, third, or fourth day can inflict injury.
Neither malaria caused by wind, nor that caused by *yāma*, nor that caused by jaundice (*pīta*) shall be able to harm them.
Even if high-ranking officials come to oppress them,
or if they are subjected to the pressure of being bound in shackles and fetters, [they shall remain unharmed].
Some have scabies or ringworm;
some develop malignant sores on their bodies or inverted flower-like ulcers;
some suffer from moist leprosy, or chronic dysentery that flares up again.
Or there may be those with red heads who cannot cause harm;
all sorcery, incantations, and curses cannot cause harm;
and all rites involving the raising of corpses cannot cause harm.
Some were created by devas, some by nāgas,
some by yakṣas, some by rākṣasas;
some were created by those suffering from thirst-disease feigning illness, or by those feigning madness.
Or various illnesses resulting from past karma may arise, yet they shall be unable to cause harm—
whether it be afflictions of the eyes, afflictions of the ears,
or afflictions of the lips, teeth, or tongue.
"Ānanda, I have now briefly explained all those who are oppressed by suffering,
with the sole exception of those experiencing the retribution for karma created through past calamities.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
I shall now further proclaim the dhāraṇī verses:
*na-tsa-ve ku-na-tsa-ve na-tsa-me mi-pa-ra-na-ta-ga-se pa-ra-ga-se svāhā*. The past Buddhas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
I have already spoken these dhāraṇī verses.
Ānanda, if there should be anyone who receives and maintains this dhāraṇī, recites it, explains it to others,
and proclaims it without forgetting, [they shall attain great merit].
That person will not be harmed by swords or staves;
no poisons, charms, or any diseases shall be able to harm them.
They shall suffer no ailments of the head.
No human or non-human being shall commit evil;
even if they consume poisonous medicine, it shall turn into delicious food.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī:
Tāṭe tāṭe, kime tāṭe, kila hulu hulu mūlu mūlu gīri me ti rame svāhā ānanda. If there is anyone...
If one reads and recites these verses, upholds them, and explains them to others,
that person cannot be harmed by swords or staves;
amidst all calamities and difficulties, they shall neither be bound nor sink.
If one recites this mantra while tying it onto a cord worn as a sash,
no diseases of cold or fever shall be able to harm them.
All poisons and toxins shall be cured immediately upon the recitation of the mantra.
Furthermore, Ānanda, I shall further proclaim the dhāraṇī verses for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, to increase their merit,
to increase their majestic power, and to increase their physical beauty.
Because it increases renown, because it increases power,
because one experiences pleasure according to one's wishes, because one experiences peace and happiness in accordance with one's conduct,
because there is no agitation, because there is no killing or harming, and because there is protection.
And he spoke the mantra, saying:
*Tadyathā | Āvayāvaye vigate* |
Vajrapāṇi, aparyantadhare, nilūpakarame, anagure, akulaviśvate, anavilābhivrate, anagure.
Abhikāra-kṣiṇe abhibuddhe akūpe ajude śubhade tite jayopade.
Mahādevī upaśami medatā parādhideva duḥśama ni.
Araṭa dhāriṣvati dhāriṣva abhi-vaśamaya svāhā.
Lu-di seng-qi-duo-lo ti-a-lo-tuo seng-qi-di a-mi-duo-po-luo-bie.
Vare saravare siddhe.
Śūdi śuve upa bha va bha de va.
Vāsava viśamāpraśugisama-cchidye.
Anuparivartaka-buddhadhīśānti-śīlavṛddhi-jñānavṛddhi.
Abhidevaja-rana-dhi-akṣa-dhi.
Ajagīparāvejagīviśudhaye anadhigamaniye asaṃgaliye,
who shatters all the power of Māra’s hosts and subdues all heterodox teachers.
"May the torch of Dharma gather in and sustain all practices. Svāhā!
Ānanda, this mantra is called the 'Dhāraṇī Chapter for Purifying and Removing All Obstructions.'"
These words and phrases were spoken by the Buddhas of the three periods of time to reveal all dharmas;
if one can recite these chapters and phrases, [one shall attain liberation].
This is the mantra for immediately eliminating all demons.
I, [Name], by means of this mantra,
protect [Name] and demarcate the boundary for [Name].
Protect such-and-such a person; guard and sustain such-and-such a person.
Nurture and raise such-and-such a person to serve as a means for averting calamities.
Eliminate all illnesses, destroy all poisons, and remove wind-related disorders.
If there is a disease or ulcer below the navel accompanied by heart pain;
or if there is abdominal pain, or back pain,
or pain in the lower body, or pain in the waist, or pain in the various joints.
Whether it be all manner of pains in the shins,
knees, hips, or thighs, or again, pains in the upper parts such as the head,
eyes, or ears, or in the teeth, tongue, lips, mouth, throat, or neck;
The mantra completely pacifies all ailments of the two flanks, shoulders, both hands, and all joints,
as well as all diseases of cold and heat.
Whether it be those produced in one day, two days, three or four days—
such as diseases of wind, bile, phlegm, or a combination of these—
I shall now completely eliminate them all, restoring them to their original state.
May [these afflictions] be forever severed; may they be dispersed and extinguished without remainder, utterly consumed and brought to an end.
Should any remain, may they all be scattered and exhausted.
As for those that are not yet matured, may they immediately reach maturity and then be dispersed and cured.
If a swelling is about to erupt, may it immediately dissolve by the power of this aspiration.
Then he spoke these verses:
By the power of all Buddhas, And the power of all Arhats.
By the majestic power of all dharmas, I protect this patient with my mantra:
may they be auspicious at midnight, may they be auspicious by day,
may they be auspicious at all times, and may their entire family and kin be auspicious.
The Four Great Kings of the four quarters, who protect and sustain the world—
Vaiśravaṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, and Virūpākṣa,
together with their retinues— possess the most supreme and majestic spiritual power.
May this place be auspicious; may the deity of Vipaśyin Buddha protect the sick person.
By the spiritual power of Śikhin Buddha, who has compassion for all beings, may that deity protect you.
The protective deity Viśvabhū, the protective deity Krakucchanda who has compassion for all beings— may those deities protect you.
The protective deity Kanakamuni, the protective deity Kāśyapa Buddha.
Compassionate toward all beings, those deities protect you;
The Honored One Śākyamuni, and all deities who protect and have compassion for all beings— may those deities protect you.
The Bodhisattvas who are to be reborn in their next life,
and all the various deities who have compassion for all beings— may those deities protect you,
as do the protective deities of Akṣobhya Buddha and Vairocana.
Out of compassion for all beings, may those deities protect you:
The Buddha Śākyamuni and the Buddha Amitāyus—
may those deities protect your life, And may you live for a hundred autumns.
At that time, those two bodhisattvas,
acting as messengers from the Buddha Supreme Lamp of the East,
addressed Śākyamuni Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, we too now wish to proclaim a dhāraṇī mantra:
Tadyathā | ūve | lūve | khele | mele | śūle | nare | muke | phuḥ | svāhā. The efficacy of this mantra is as described above.”
The Buddha told Ānanda: "Ānanda, if you encounter the peril of bandits, you should mindfully recite these dhāraṇī verses.
If you find yourself among enemies, you should mindfully recite them."
One should maintain mindfulness when amidst a great fire;
one should maintain mindfulness when amidst rivers, oceans, great floods, or other such calamities;
and one should maintain mindfulness when within the jurisdiction of government officials.
One should keep in mind all difficulties arising from strife, contention, and litigation.
If a person, amidst such various calamities as these, recollects [the name] with a sincere heart,
they shall immediately be delivered from all these hardships.
Such various calamities as these cannot cause harm.
Even if the poisonous drugs of others should enter one's body,
they will immediately transform into food and be unable to cause injury.
If there is anyone who recites these dharani verses at the time when the sun first rises,
and continues to recite these dharani verses until the time of midday;
If one recites these dhāraṇī verses at the time of sunset,
or is able to recite these dhāraṇī verses at all times,
that person shall immediately be liberated from all calamities and hardships.
Ānanda, I speak these essential words for you:
if there is anyone who recites these verses of this dhāraṇī,
upholds, reads, and recites them, and explains them to others.
It is impossible for that person to encounter any place of fear,
whether among government officials or within a band of robbers.
Or they may be burned by fire, or swept away and drowned by water;
or they may be seized by various nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas,
great ghost generals, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, and piśācas.
Pretas, asuras, kumbhāṇḍas, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras; the maladies of parching thirst and delirium;
feigning madness, sorcery, and the raising of corpse-demons;
and the diseases of chills and fever that manifest once a day, or those that manifest every second, third, or fourth day.
Those caused by the moon deity, those caused by the sun deity, and those caused by the lunar mansions;
lions, tigers, wolves, jackals, brown bears, leopards, and the like;
as well as poisonous charms, wicked dogs, pythons, snakes, vipers, centipedes, scorpions, and the like.
No venomous insects, humans, or non-humans shall be able to cause them fear.
If anyone receives and upholds these words and phrases of the dhāraṇī, [they shall be thus protected].
All ghosts and spirits, all yakṣas, all rākṣasas, all ghost generals, and all kumbhāṇḍas—
all hungry ghosts— will be unable to cause harm.
No fears from humans or non-humans can subdue them.
Ānanda, if there is anyone who recites these verses of this dhāraṇī,
those facing death may be released from the scourging of whips and staves.
Those who deserve to be flogged or caned shall instead pay a small amount of wealth;
those who deserve to pay wealth shall instead be released through humiliation;
those who deserve to be reviled and rebuked shall instead be released.
They should be rebuked so that they may immediately attain liberation.
Ānanda, if there are those who read and recite these dharani verses, uphold them, and explain them for others;
or if they rejoice in them with their hearts, or contemplate them with discernment day and night.
Fire cannot burn that person; blades and clubs cannot wound them;
water cannot drown them; poisons cannot kill them;
and sorcery cannot harm them.
Ānanda, I have spoken to you in brief.
Within the world of gods and humans, I do not see anyone—
whether among the Brahmā worlds or among the world of śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas— who [surpasses me].
Whether it be against the world of Māras, Asuras,
and so forth, one may use these dharani phrases as a protection;
whether for establishing a boundary or for averting calamities.
It is impossible for the mind to become disturbed or for there to be fear. Why is this so?
Because all Buddhas uphold this dhāraṇī,
they immediately transcend all calamities and difficulties.
Ānanda, if there are those who recite this dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain such benefits].
If there is a tree about to wither and dry up,
whether one recites a mantra for that tree or establishes a boundary (sīmābandha) for it,
at that time the tree will once again produce branches, twigs, leaves, flowers, fruits, and so forth.
If it can be restored to its original state,
how much more so for a human being endowed with consciousness— would it not be impossible for such a person not to recover?
Is there no such possibility?
Except for the retribution of karmic fruits resulting from past calamities.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings rose from their seats for the last time and adjusted their robes.
Baring his right shoulder and placing his right knee upon the ground,
he joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
I shall now also speak the dhāraṇī verses."
Blessed One, if there should be anyone who upholds and recollects [this],
and for the sake of explaining, proclaiming, and manifesting it to others, we shall act as guardians and protectors for that person.
Out of compassion and loving-kindness, we shall speak these dhāraṇī verses for the sake of that Dharma-preacher.
Furthermore, for the sake of protecting and upholding this fundamental dharma,
may this fundamental dharma abide long in the world,
subduing all māras and closing off all heterodox paths.
"Those Dharma-preachers desire that their longevity, physical strength, eloquence, and fearlessness may increase.
World-Honored One, if you would grant us permission, we shall speak.
At that time, the World-Honored One granted his consent by remaining silent.
The Heavenly King, seeing that the Buddha remained silent and had granted his internal approval, immediately recited these dhāraṇī verses:

Tadyathā | Tātātātāti | Tātātāti | Dhātadhātāti | Dhātadhātāti | Dhābadhābadhā | Cakre | Vaidhe | Vaidhe | Dandini | Mahādandini | Danda | Jambhani | Stambhani | Mahāstambhani | Kuṭṭani | Mahākuṭṭani | Cañcale | Malle | Malle | Māmale | Svāhā. "World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī of ours—"
To protect and uphold this internal exposition of the fundamental mind,
the Blessed One said: "If there should be anyone who receives and upholds this dhāraṇī,
reciting it again and again, or explaining it to others."
They shall be entirely free from fear and there shall be no place for them to be harmed.
No beings whatsoever who follow that person shall be able to create obstacles,
because they have mastered and protected all dharmas.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, you and your kind!
You are able to bring great benefit to many people."
"You are able to bring peace and happiness to many people;
you are able to protect and sustain gods and humans.
Within this world, you all must uphold the True Dharma."
Furthermore, he brings great benefit to those teachers of the Dharma,
protecting them, ensuring their peace and happiness, increasing their right mindfulness,
increasing their wisdom, and increasing their eloquence.
"You all should resolve your minds.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Regarding this dhāraṇī, it was spoken by all Buddhas of the past."
I now speak it here and now for the benefit of all sentient beings;
whoever possesses right faith and upholds these verses shall always know their past lives throughout twenty-eight lifetimes.
If there are those with right faith who hear this dhāraṇī wherever they may be,
they shall obtain liberation from all fears caused by humans and non-humans, such as yakṣas and kumbhāṇḍas.
Pūtana spirits and the like cannot create obstacles;
if one recites this mantra, blades and staves cannot harm them,
poisons cannot kill them, and great fires cannot burn them.
All sorcery and the like cannot drown one in the depths of water;
if one recites these verses, malevolent māras, bhūtas,
and devas of the desire realm will be unable to create obstacles.
By reciting this dhāraṇī, parents, brothers,
and all one's kinsmen and retinue shall not be seen to suffer separation;
by reading and reciting these verses, all matters shall be auspicious.
If one has committed evil offenses throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas,
by reciting this mantra for seven days, all [those offenses] can be completely extinguished and eliminated.
[Likewise,] the merits accumulated by all Bodhisattvas throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas—
Within these seven days, there are no distinctions among the four great heavenly kings;
from the four directions they come here—
Vaiśravaṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, and Virūpākṣa.
Together with their retinues, possessing exquisite forms and great majesty,
by the power of this mantra, they shall protect that Dharma teacher. At that time,
the World-Honored One addressed the Elder Ānanda, saying:
Ānanda, you should receive and uphold these root verses of this dhāraṇī method.
Ānanda, this root method shall bring great benefit;
it possesses great efficacy and great power.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One,
I shall receive and uphold these verses and phrases so that they are never forgotten or lost.
The Buddha then spoke these verses and phrases of the dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Elder Ānanda,
along with that assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
and those two bodhisattvas who had come from other directions, [were present].
Śakra-devānām-indra, the Great Brahmā-deva, the Four Great Kings,
along with the great assembly of devas, asuras, gandharvas, mahoragas, and others.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
*The Sūtra of the Tathāgata Supreme Lamp King of the East*.
